original_test_intent: Stress host DDR memory with the source-defined stress-ng virtual-memory workload for eight hours and verify continued platform health without memory or system-event errors.

original_procedure_criteria.procedure: Install stress-ng, clear dmesg, run `stress-ng -m 15 --vm 9 --vm-bytes 90% -t 8h`, then inspect logs.
original_procedure_criteria.criteria: SUT remains workable, no badblock is reported, and no system event error appears.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Reduced the source-specific workload to a generic memory-allocation description.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Preserved eight hours and 90% but identified duplicate worker options as unresolved.
historical_reviews.v3: REWRITE_REQUIRED; proved `-m` and `--vm` are aliases and required one owner-selected worker count.

v3_1_conclusion.manual_test_activity: Engineering resolves the conflicting worker count and approves capacity, thresholds, package and recovery; the approved workload and collection are automatable.
required_user_inputs: Installed stress-ng version and allocation semantics
RAM error/workable acceptance and safety thresholds

master_vs_project_parameters.master_default: Eight hours, 90% allocation intent, and the unresolved source values 15 and 9 are retained verbatim.
master_vs_project_parameters.project_inputs: One approved worker count, exact tool version, capacity/NUMA/swap constraints and thresholds.
master_vs_project_parameters.coverage_difference: A shorter or lower-pressure approved run completes only that project plan; the master eight-hour/90% gap remains visible.

original_method: Retain the original stress-ng command as source evidence but do not execute it unchanged because two aliases specify different worker counts.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: After owner resolution, use one option: `stress-ng --vm <APPROVED_WORKERS> --vm-bytes 90% --timeout 8h`, preferably through an existing approved monitor/wrapper.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Installed project-qualified stress-ng release; validate local help before execution.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Upstream stress-ng(1) manual, with installed-version semantics controlling execution.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original: Removes the contradictory alias assignment without choosing the missing engineering value.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: None if the approved worker value represents the intended source workload; otherwise record the project override.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: High allocation can cause OOM, swap pressure, thermal/power stress or loss of control.

missing_inputs: Package source/version, limits and recovery owner
safety_boundaries: No execution of the ambiguous command and no guessing option precedence.
Dedicated capacity, monitoring, abort and OOB recovery are mandatory.
expected_evidence: Approved corrected command and version semantics
Full stress output, elapsed time and exit status
no_automatic_retry: Preserve any OOM, hang, early stop or error. A changed worker count or allocation is a new plan requiring approval, not an automatic retry.
engineer_owned_verdict: Agent records execution and evidence; engineer resolves the source conflict and decides the formal result.
review_improvement: V3 already handled the command defect correctly. V3.1 keeps that conclusion while clarifying that duration and pressure are Master Defaults that a project may override only with an explicit coverage delta; it does not relax the unresolved-command safety gate.
